references.text: The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to a settled land – they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
Refers to the forty years in the wilderness as a consequence of the people's disobedience, where each year corresponded to a day the spies were in the land.
Mentions that Aaron died in the fortieth year after the Israelites had left Egypt, marking the end of the wilderness journey.
Parallel text describing the forty years in the wilderness and specifically noting that their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
Nehemiah repeats this miracle and confirms that for forty years in the wilderness they lacked nothing; their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
Amos refers to the forty years God led Israel through the wilderness to take possession of the land of the Amorites.
Stephen mentions in his speech that Moses led the people out and performed signs and wonders for forty years in the wilderness.
Paul refers to the forty years God put up with the people of Israel in the wilderness.
The book of Hebrews asks whom God was angry with for forty years, and answers that it was those who sinned and fell in the wilderness.
